params.script_inline:
import sys, json

# A scriptlet ships BLANK on purpose: it hands the turns it was given straight
# back, and whatever it should do instead arrives as `script_inline` in the
# override_params of the declaration that instantiates it. That is the whole
# template -- a `code` cell with a name, a runner and no opinion of its own.
#
# The three objects on stdin are always set, even when empty: `envelope` (what
# the substrate wraps around the payload -- header, target, trace_id, ttl),
# `body` (the message's own slots) and `params` (this cell's configuration,
# minus credentials and minus this script). Read the payload out of `body`.
# Never win it by subtracting a hardcoded list of envelope keys: that is the
# error class the three-object form was built to end.
#
# stdout is one content JSON -- an optional `header` section the colony reads
# as `hop`, plus the body slots. `context` is edge authority and is never
# written here. This template declares `multi_send_capable`, so a replacement
# script may write a JSON ARRAY instead and emit one message per element.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
body = doc["body"]
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"messages": body.get("messages") or []}))

description.purpose: A script a manifest can name: one code cell as a whole template, shipped BLANK -- it hands its turns straight back, and the logic arrives as `script_inline` in the override_params of the declaration that instantiates it. Five shipped templates hold a single code cell (door, terminal, retry, dispatcher, archive-bridge) and every one of them carries a script and a purpose of its own; this one carries neither, which is the point.
description.use_when: Wherever a topology needs application logic between two cells: reshaping a body, extracting the calls out of an answer, turning one message into many. Instantiate it under a name that says what it does and hand it its script in the same declaration.
description.not_in_scope: No cell.db -- a code cell has none, so state that has to survive a message goes to a store over the topology, not into a variable. No sandbox key either: a cell instantiated without one gets the default-deny profile, and this template does not declare the key, so a manifest cannot widen it through here. No opinion about the wire: what the replacement script emits is what leaves.
description.emits_meaning: Whatever the script writes on stdout, validated against contract.emits ALWAYS-ON -- a code cell is the one user-script-driven trust boundary, so an emission missing messages[] comes back as contract_violation rather than travelling. The cell stamps exit_code, duration_ms and had_stderr itself and a script cannot hijack them; every other hop key is the script's word.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: the turns of the inbound message. The whole message reaches the script as three stdin objects -- envelope, body, params -- and the shipped script reads body.messages and writes it back unchanged.
examples: the shipped script: any message in -> the same messages[] out, hop { exit_code: 0, duration_ms: 12 }
override_params {"script_inline": "..."} -> the same template, a different cell; that override is what makes a manifest ask its colony the `code.author` question
a replacement script writing a JSON array -> one outbound message per element, each evaluated against this cell's edges independently
